raw_response:
I've been working this land for forty years. I know what Quzhou's soil and weather demand. My sons and daughter-in-law work in the city, so I need to keep things manageable — I can't be running the sprayer every other week like I used to. But I won't cut corners either. Let me think through each crop.

**Wheat (winter, ~10 mu):** I'll plant Jimai 22 again — it's reliable here, the neighbors all use it. I put down compound fertilizer at sowing and top-dress urea at jointing. I always irrigate before winter, again at jointing, and at heading — three times is usually enough unless spring is dry, then I do a fourth. I'll spray once for aphids and once for rust, same as always. After maize harvest I use the rotary tiller to chop the stalks into the soil.

**Maize (summer, same 10 mu):** Right after I cut wheat in June, I drill maize into the stubble — no-tillage saves my back and time. I use Zhengdan 958, proven hybrid. I top-dress twice with urea. I need to water at emergence if it's dry, and again at silking. Corn borer is the main pest — one or two sprays covers it.

**Cotton (6.9 mu, separate plot):** Cotton is more work but the price has held up. I'll use an improved Bt variety to keep bollworm spraying down. Cotton needs more potassium than the grain crops. I irrigate at flowering and boll setting mostly. I'll still spray 4 times — aphids early, then bollworm even with Bt, then spider mites in August. I'll plough this field in spring before transplanting.
